text: The wizard raised his sword as the dragon circled the kingdom. Only an ancient spell could save the realm from the dark magic that bled across the land.
label: Fantasy
convention: Dense, unambiguous fantasy iconography (wizard, sword, dragon, kingdom, spell, realm, magic) — a competent human reads this as Fantasy, and the keyword scorer agrees.

text: The ship's engine coughed once before the jump. Beyond the station's viewport, the planet turned slow against a field of stars, and the galaxy seemed to hold its breath.
label: Sci-Fi
convention: Space-opera setting (ship, engine, station, planet, galaxy) reads as Sci-Fi to a human; scorer also lands Sci-Fi.

text: The detective knelt by the body. Every clue pointed to the same suspect, but the evidence in this case refused to add up; somewhere, a murderer was still breathing.
label: Mystery
convention: Whodunit framing (detective, body, clue, suspect, evidence, case, murder) is Mystery by genre convention; scorer agrees.

text: She felt her heart stumble when he leaned close. A blush rose to her cheeks; the longing in his eyes mirrored her own as they fell into an embrace and a single, trembling kiss.
label: Romance
convention: Emotional intimacy beats (heart, blush, longing, embrace, kiss) are Romance; scorer agrees.

text: The agent sprinted, gun drawn, as the chase spilled into the station. Her target had a bomb, and the hostage had minutes to live before the whole platform went up.
label: Thriller
convention: High-stakes pursuit (agent, gun, chase, target, bomb, hostage) reads as Thriller; the lone Sci-Fi false hit (station) is outweighed, so scorer agrees.

text: Blood pooled beneath the door. In the dark, something scraped — a creature, or the corpse it had left to haunt the cellar where the screams had stopped.
label: Horror
convention: Visceral dread (blood, dark, creature, corpse, haunt, scream) is Horror; scorer agrees.

text: The afternoon thinned to a pale gold over the orchard. She sat on the porch with the unopened letter in her lap, watching the wind turn the long grass, and did not move for a long while.
label: none
convention: Quiet literary interiority with no genre markers at all — a human declines to assign a bucket; scorer finds zero keywords and returns none.

text: They repainted the hallway on Saturday. Tom held the ladder; Priya argued about the shade of grey until they both gave up and ordered pizza.
label: none
convention: Mundane domestic vignette, no genre vocabulary; human says none, scorer scores zero and returns none.

text: El ingeniero revisó el motor del taller antes del amanecer. La relación entre los dos pueblos llevaba años rota, y nadie quería ser el primero en ceder.
label: none
convention: Spanish realist passage about an engineer and feuding towns — no genre. Doubles as a substring-safety check: 'ingeniero', 'motor', 'relación' do not contain the English substrings engine/ship, so the scorer correctly returns none.

text: The lead engineer wiped grease from her hands. The relationship between the two township councils had soured over who would pay for the staircase repairs in the old bookcase factory.
label: none
convention: A human reads a workplace/civic vignette with no genre at all. The substring scorer counts engine (engineer), ship (relationship), ship (township) = 3 Sci-Fi and case (staircase, bookcase) = 2 Mystery, so it wrongly outputs Sci-Fi.

text: "Darling," she said, exasperated, "you spell everything wrong." He grinned, unbothered, and kept writing the grocery list at the kitchen table.
label: none
convention: Word-sense trap: 'spell' here is the verb 'to spell', and the scene is plainly domestic — a human assigns none. The scorer matches the literal substring 'spell' and outputs Fantasy.

text: The wizard's spell tore the dark open and something with no face climbed out. Blood ran down the kingdom's white walls as the creature screamed in a voice that was almost a word.
label: Fantasy
convention: Cross-bucket bleed: a human reads dark fantasy — the wizard/spell/kingdom world-frame is primary and the horror imagery is texture. The scorer tallies Horror 4 (blood, dark, creature, scream) over Fantasy 3 (wizard, spell, kingdom) and outputs Horror.

text: Het ruimteschip naderde de planeet bij volle snelheid. De relatie tussen de bemanningsleden werd gespannen toen de motor uitviel en de sterren stil bleven hangen.
label: Sci-Fi
convention: A human reads obvious Dutch sci-fi (ruimteschip = spaceship, planeet, bemanning, motor). The English-only keyword list matches nothing — 'schip'/'planeet'/'motor' lack the English substrings — so the scorer returns none.

text: Blut sickerte unter der Tür hervor. Im Dunkeln kratzte etwas an der Wand, und aus dem Keller stieg ein Schrei, der kein menschlicher Schrei mehr war.
label: Horror
convention: Unmistakable German horror (Blut = blood, Dunkeln = dark, Schrei = scream). The English-only scorer matches none of these German words and returns none.

text: Le détective s'agenouilla près du corps. Chaque indice menait au même suspect, mais aucune preuve ne tenait dans cette affaire de meurtre non résolu.
label: Mystery
convention: French mystery (détective, corps, indice, suspect, meurtre). A human says Mystery, and the scorer agrees by accident: the French cognate 'suspect' contains the English keyword 'suspect', and 'détective' contains 'detective', so Mystery scores highest.
